On Oct 30 2026, the SEC issued exemptive relief (Release No. 34-106789 / press release 2026-111) creating a capped carve-out for certain non-U.S. bilateral repo and inter-affiliate transactions, but no compliance date was moved. Commissioner Uyeda at the Sept 22 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference stated the SEC 'does not currently intend to extend these deadlines.' (Sources: sec.gov; theindustryspread.com Oct 31 2026; beaumont-capitalmarkets.co.uk Nov 2026)
clearing_status.rationale: Rubric 1 requires an official extension granted OR exemptive-relief requests pending: exactly one formal extension (90 FR 11134) has been granted and remains operative. The Oct 30 2026 exemptive order is a scope carve-out, not a deadline extension, so it does not trigger rubric 2; and because an extension has been granted, rubric 0 is excluded.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 (April 4, 2025) — imposing case-by-case export licensing on seven medium/heavy rare earths (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y) and derivative magnets (NdFeB, SmCo) — remains fully in force and was not included in the suspension under Announcement No. 70. Processing times run 45 days to several months with no statutory deadline. General licences issued to named producers (JL MAG, BZSAN, Yunsheng) are scoped to specific downstream customers, not blanket coverage. The October 2025 expanded controls (Nos. 55-58, 61, 62) suspension nominally expires November 10, 2026; a September 28, 2026 MOFCOM official statement suggests extension to January 10, 2027, but no formal numbered amendment to Announcement 70 had been published as of October 28, 2026 (monoscope-media.com, mainrichinternational.com, carraglobe.com, checked Oct 28 2026).
license_flow.rationale: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 constitutes active case-by-case (whitelist) licensing with processing times routinely exceeding 30 days — squarely meeting the rubric definition of value 1 (SLOWING). No categorical denial or suspension of licensing issuance has been announced, so value 2 is not warranted; no blanket/general licence covers most export volume at sub-30-day processing, so value 0 is excluded.

dissent.view: Carraglobe and technology.org (Oct 14-19, 2026) note that as of their check dates, no formal numbered MOFCOM announcement extending Announcement 70 beyond November 10, 2026 had been published, suggesting the expanded October controls could legally snap back; however this concerns the suspended layer (Nos. 55-58, 61-62), not the operative Announcement 18 case-by-case regime, and does not change the rubric value.

Mainrich International (Oct 11, 2026) and carraglobe (Oct 14, 2026) report a MOFCOM official September 28, 2026 statement extending the broader Busan arrangement to January 10, 2027, which some read as covering the rare earth suspension — but the statement does not name rare earths and no amendment to Announcement 70 has been formally issued.

ss_reform_news.rationale: The Trustees Report materially worsened the depletion timeline and reform is actively debated in multiple bills, satisfying Band 1 (DEBATE). The two new post-10/26 enacted laws are administrative/nomenclature measures that do not alter the trust-fund outlook.

dissent.view: CBO (Feb 2026) projects a sharper 26-28% cut and slightly earlier mid-2032 depletion vs. SSA Trustees' 22% and Q4 2032 -- a more pessimistic read on the same rubric band, still Band 1

funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the canonical large-US-public-pension funded ratio series; the October 28, 2026 release reports 87.4% as of September 30, 2026, which is the latest measured data point and maps directly to the rubric. This supersedes the prior 88.2% (July 31, 2026) reading as a new post-cutoff event.
funded_ratio.change_reason: new_event: Milliman PPFI October 28, 2026 release shows funded ratio fell to 87.4% as of September 30, 2026, down from 88.2% at July 31, driven by a -1.4% monthly return in September that erased $112 billion in funded status.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up: 2026 Edition (data workbook May 2026, PDF June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): 'The median project built in 2025 took 61 months from the interconnection request to commercial operations' — down from 63 months for the 2024 in-service cohort.
interconnection_months.rationale: The most recent authoritative LBNL primary source (Queued Up 2026 Edition, data through end-2025, published May/June 2026) confirms the median IR-to-COD for the 2025 in-service cohort is exactly 61 months, identical to the prior reading. No new LBNL edition or updated data workbook superseding this figure has been published since June 2026.

dc_moratoria.fact: electricchoice.com (updated ~Oct 2026) tracks '575 currently in force across 46 states'; NY Gov. Hochul signed EO 62 on Jul 14, 2026 — the first confirmed statewide moratorium, still in force; 11 additional governors (VA, PA, MA, KY, OH, TX, NV, OR, UT, NE, LA) have signed restricting executive orders/directives; hundreds of enacted local/county moratoria confirmed across NJ (93), OH (55+), GA, NC, CA, FL, IN, KY, and others (electricchoice.com; quorum.us Oct 2026; datacenterbans.com Oct 2026).
dc_moratoria.rationale: NY's statewide moratorium via EO 62 alone satisfies the '>= 1 statewide moratorium enacted' threshold for value=2; additionally, the count of jurisdictions with enacted pauses is confirmed well above 10 across dozens of states, further meeting the '>10 jurisdictions' alternative threshold.

dissent.view: Quorum (Oct 2026) notes NY is the only statewide moratorium and 'no state has enacted a moratorium by statute as of October 2026; Maine's legislature passed one but the governor vetoed it' — this is consistent with the reading (EO 62 is executive, not statutory), so no conflict on the rubric outcome.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE Order No. 202-26-50 (Oct 12-16, 2026) expired without triggering an EEA-3 or confirmed data-center curtailment - PJM stated 'no customer impacts' were needed. FERC on Oct 9, 2026 rejected PJM's IRAS mandatory curtailment framework (ER26-3515). No new Section 202(c) emergency order has been issued as of Nov 2, 2026. Structural tightness persists: PJM projects capacity shortfall from 2027-28 delivery year; data-center pipeline ~67 GW by 2036; interconnection queues remain long. Source: DOE energy.gov (Oct 12-16 order); FERC docket ER26-3515 (Oct 9); PJM spokesperson via Newsweek (Oct 15); Daily Caller / tech-insider.org (Oct 14-15, 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires confirmed curtailment, a declared grid emergency, or an active moratorium; the Oct 12-16 order authorized curtailment as a last resort but PJM confirmed it was not invoked, and the order has now lapsed with no successor. Level 1 fits: interconnection queues remain long and lengthening, projects are delayed for power, repeated emergency orders throughout 2026 document structural tightness, but no curtailment has been confirmed active as of today.
ai_power_pressure.change_reason: new_event: DOE Order No. 202-26-50 expired Oct 16 2026 without confirmed data-center curtailment (PJM: 'no customer impacts'); FERC Oct 9 2026 rejected PJM IRAS mandatory curtailment framework; no new 202(c) emergency order issued as of Nov 2 2026 - active level-2 trigger has lapsed

dissent.view: Some sources characterize the Oct 12-16 PJM emergency order itself as a level-2 event (grid emergency declared) regardless of whether EEA-3 was actually reached, which would sustain a value of 2.
FERC's Oct 9 rejection of PJM curtailment rules means PJM formally lacks standing authority to cut data-center power, arguably pushing conditions back toward level 1 structurally.

mine_disruptions.fact: Grasberg Block Cave throughput averaged ~141,000 t/day in Q3 2026 = 67% of normal capacity (Freeport 8-K Oct 27 2026; SMM Oct 28 2026); Indonesian operations produced 249 Mlb copper in Q3 vs ~311 Mlb in Q3 2025, with full-capacity restart pushed to end-2027/early 2028. Kamoa-Kakula produced 76,401 t saleable copper in Q3 2026 with 2026 guidance of 290,000-310,000 t trending to lower end vs ~380,000-400,000 t design capacity; smelter at ~60% of 500,000 t/yr design (Ivanhoe Q3 release, Oct 8 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Two top-3 copper mines remain in confirmed production shortfalls: Grasberg at 67% capacity with ~35% annual output loss vs pre-incident (Goldman/BMI forecast >400,000 t 2026 market deficit attributable largely to this), and Kamoa-Kakula tracking ~25% below design-capacity guidance. This exceeds the rubric threshold of >=2 major mines disrupted with institutional deficit forecasts confirmed.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG October 2026 biannual forecast (issued 14-15 Oct 2026): global refined copper market surplus of ~104,000 metric tons in 2026, widening to ~368,000 mt in 2027. Source: Mining Weekly (15 Oct 2026): 'The International Copper Study Group forecast on Wednesday that the global refined copper market would remain in surplus through 2027, with it widening from about 104 000 metric tons in 2026 to 368 000 metric tons in 2027.'
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: ICSG's official latest forecast is a 104,000 mt refined surplus for 2026, well above zero and clearly on the surplus side. Rubric band 0 (SURPLUS) applies: official forecast is a surplus, not within +/-100kt of balance.

drought_chip_farm.fact: Taiwan WRA live data (wra.gov.tw, Oct 31 2026): Tsengwen reservoir 88.06%, Wushantou 87.06%, Te-Chi 98.05%, Sun-Moon-Lake 96.84%, Shimen 100% — all near or above normal, no rationing order in force. US Southwest: USDM National Drought Summary (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, data valid Oct 27 2026, released Oct 29 2026) states 'continued pattern of robust precipitation through most of the West Region led to continued improvement'; New Mexico (representative SW farm/chip corridor) had ~25% area in D2-D4 as of Oct 20 data, with improvement trend continuing into late October.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Taiwan reservoirs are fully recovered with no rationing — does not meet rubric level 2 or even level 1 criteria on its own. US Southwest retains residual D2 (severe drought) coverage in areas like New Mexico, satisfying the rubric's level-1 threshold ('severe D2 drought'), but no D3/D4 dominates chip-fab or major farm hubs and no rationing order is in force, keeping the rating at 1 rather than 2.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,038.85 ft, storage 6,898,730 acre-feet, 26.4% of USBR active capacity (26,120,000 AF basis) as of Oct 31, 2026 — an all-time record low (previous record 1,040.5 ft on Jul 28, 2022); minimum power pool is 950 ft, reservoir ~89 ft above that threshold. Source: USBR RISE daily gauge data via coloradorivermonitor.com and reservoirbench.com (Oct 31, 2026).
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.4% of USBR active capacity, Lake Mead is firmly below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold. The reservoir also set a new all-time record low on Oct 22, 2026 (1,037.16 ft), confirming a confirmed physical impact; it remains ~89 ft above minimum power pool (950 ft), well within the rubric's 'within 15 ft' sub-criterion but the <30% storage criterion is independently met.

dissent.view: lakelevelnow.com reports 24% full using max capacity ~28.95M AF basis vs USBR active capacity 26.12M AF used by coloradorivermonitor.com (26.4%); both are below 30% so rubric outcome is identical.

water_dispute.fact: Pakistan Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gillani, speaking at Pakistan Water Week 2026 in Islamabad on 2 November 2026, declared 'Any attempt to block or divert Pakistan\'s share of water will be treated as an act of war,' reaffirming PM Shehbaz Sharif\'s identical formulation on 21 October 2026; India\'s IWT abeyance remains in force and India has rejected the PCA\'s 31 August 2026 ruling that the treaty is binding (Arab News Pakistan, 2 Nov 2026; Pakistan Today, 21 Oct 2026; Al Jazeera, 1 Sep 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: India\'s unilateral IWT abeyance (a standing treaty-suspension condition = Level 1 floor) is compounded by explicit, repeated \'act of war\' declarations from Pakistan\'s head of government (PM Sharif, 21 Oct) and Senate Chairman (Gillani, 2 Nov) within the last 90 days, meeting the rubric\'s Level 2 threshold of an explicit threat of war over a dam/river by a head of state or government. No armed clash or physical flow cut-off has occurred, but the explicit war threat criterion is satisfied by qualifying officials.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 2.0 points (+1.5%) MoM from revised August 2026 and +5.8% YoY; third consecutive monthly increase and highest reading since November 2022. Source: FAO (fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex), released 2 October 2026. October 2026 reading not yet published (scheduled 6 November 2026).
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM rise of +1.5% is above zero (rising) but below the 3% threshold for band 1 and well below the 5% spike threshold; 3-month cumulative gain (July 131.1 → September 136.0) is ~+3.7%, below the 10% SPIKING threshold — squarely in band 1 (ELEVATED).

china_export_curbs.fact: China Customs data for September 2026 (SunSirs/ChemNet, cited ~Oct 19 2026) shows DAP exports of 70,000 t (-97.1% YoY) and MAP of 110,000 t (-90.9% YoY); Argus Media data cited by global-agriculture.com (Oct 19 2026) confirms phosphate exports have fallen from 5.3 mln t in 2025 to 'almost nothing' in 2026. Phosphate export declarations technically resumed Sep 1 (keyuanfertilizer.com) but remain under quota/license management with regulator right to readjust; urea under quota self-discipline allocation (MOFCOM). No new restriction broadening since Oct 19.
china_export_curbs.rationale: Restrictions remain in place across phosphate (quota/license-controlled, near-zero physical flows) and urea (quota system), satisfying rubric level 1. No new or broadened measure was introduced in the trailing 3 months (Aug-Nov 2026) to justify level 2.

dissent.view: SMM Flash (Aug 2026) reported phosphate export declarations would resume 'normally' from Sep 1, implying a possible move toward level 0; however customs data and Argus/global-agriculture.com confirm physical exports remain near zero under continued quota/license controls, negating any full lifting.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 2 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on October 25, 2026 — the latest published PortWatch data point — against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85 per day, equalling ~2% of baseline. Source: straits.live daily brief Nov 2, 2026 (sourcing portwatch.imf.org); corroborated by hormuz.now live tracker Nov 2, 2026 showing a November 2026 average of 9.0/day from independent AIS counts.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: 2 transits/day is ~2% of the ~85/day pre-crisis baseline, far below the rubric's 25% threshold for CUT (value=2). The transit collapse is ongoing and uninterrupted since the last reading, with no recovery event recorded.

dissent.view: hormuz.now independent AIS (not IMF PortWatch) counts ~9 transits/day for November 2026 so far and 9 on Nov 1 — still only ~11% of baseline, which also maps to value=2 under the rubric.

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan MND X post (26 Oct 2026, covering to 0600 UTC+8): '3 sorties of PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships operating around Taiwan detected up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today. 1 out of 3 sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwan\'s southwestern and eastern part ADIZ. ROC Armed Forces have monitored the situation and responded.' No new named large-scale PLA encirclement exercise announced post-26 Oct; Oct 12-17 coastal live-fire drills (5 zones, not near Taiwan) concluded. Taiwan MND warned of Nov-Dec PLA drill peak season but no exercise launched as of search date. Source: Taiwan MND via ANI/Tribune India, 26 Oct 2026.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent daily ADIZ incursions with median-line crossings and sustained PLAN vessel presence fit rubric level 1 (elevated assertive patrols) but no kinetic clash, no named blockade-rehearsal encirclement drill, and no full mobilization places this below level 2. The Oct 12-17 coastal drills have concluded and no new major exercise has been confirmed post-26 Oct.

export_controls.fact: Between Oct 13-19 2026, MOFCOM issued a package of new dual-use export-control measures (UAVs, tunnel boring machines, dredgers) effective Nov 18 2026, supplementing the Oct 16 Announcement No. 48 (40-technology draft controls on AI/chips/solar, interim registration in force). China's Jun 2026 dual-use bans on 10 US companies and Jul 24 MOFCOM Announcement No. 30 (14 EU entities added to Export Control List) remain active. Source: akingump.com (Oct 19 2026); geopolitechs.org / cms.law (Jul 24 2026); pillsburylaw.com (Oct 16 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both Western controls (NL/US/EU on chip equipment) and Chinese countermeasures (entity-list bans on US/EU/Japanese firms, dual-use export bans, 40-tech draft with interim registration) are active within the trailing 90 days, satisfying rubric level 2 (RETALIATION: target country enacts countermeasures). No de-escalation or suspension of these measures has been confirmed.
export_controls.change_reason: new_event: Oct 13-19 2026 MOFCOM package of UAV/tunnel boring/dredger dual-use controls (effective Nov 18 2026) is new post-Oct-16 action that reinforces the level-2 reading without changing it

dissent.view: ASML annual report and Busan Summit context suggest a partial US-China trade truce (rare-earth suspension until Nov 10-27 2026) that has modestly reduced acute escalation pressure, which could argue for capping at 1 if the truce is read as offsetting retaliation; however, MOFCOM entity-list and dual-use bans on Western firms are not suspended and remain active countermeasures.

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC 3nm capacity ~180,000 wpm (all Taiwan) by early Q4 2026; 2nm at ~90,000 wpm end-2026 (all Taiwan). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3): equipment installation underway Q3 2026, HVM targeted H2 2027. Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm): HVM 2028. Zero <=3nm wafers produced outside Taiwan as of today. Sources: TrendForce Sept 14 2026 (via Economic Daily News); Evertiq Oct 19 2026; VentureAtlas Nov 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: 100% of operational <=3nm capacity remains in Taiwan; both overseas 3nm fabs (Arizona H2 2027, Japan 2028) are pre-production. This satisfies rubric level 2: <10% outside Taiwan AND no operational overseas leading-edge fab.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 2 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on October 25 2026 (latest published date), against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (2.4% of baseline); corroborated by straits.live brief dated 2026-11-02 citing PortWatch, and hormuz.now AIS tracker showing ~9/day for early November 2026 (still <11% of baseline); UKMTO reported a vessel struck by projectile on November 1 2026 (straits.live 2026-11-02).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Hormuz at 2-3% of baseline is far below the 25% threshold for CLOSED (rating=2) under the rubric; the Nov 1 UKMTO vessel strike confirms attacks are ongoing and active within the last 7 days, reinforcing the CLOSED classification as the worse of the two chokepoints.

dissent.view: hormuz.now AIS tracker records ~9 commercial transits/day for November 2026 so far (higher than PortWatch's 2 on Oct 25), suggesting some AIS-visible traffic is recovering slightly, but this is still only ~10% of baseline and does not change the rubric outcome

cable_incidents.fact: Reuters (Oct 24, 2026) reported, citing two senior Iranian security officials, that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to attack undersea communications cables in the Persian Gulf if US-Israeli strikes resume; IRGC political deputy Yadollah Javani publicly warned seven major cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz are legitimate targets. TeleGeography confirmed no Hormuz connectivity loss and noted less than 1% of global bandwidth transits Hormuz. No cable cut confirmed as of 2026-11-02.
cable_incidents.rationale: Credible, named official threats (IRGC/Reuters, Oct 24 2026) within the last 90 days place this squarely in rubric level 1 (THREATENED); no cable is confirmed severed and unrepaired, so level 2 is not warranted.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SEC issued final exemptive relief (Release No. 34-106789, Oct 30 2026) for certain inter-affiliate and non-U.S. repo transactions, resolving one pending exemptive-relief item; deadlines remain Dec 31 2026 (cash) and Jun 30 2027 (repo) unchanged. The load-bearing readiness data remains the SIFMA/BNY/Broadridge/DTCC pulse survey (n=340, June 2026, published Sept 22 2026): 86% at least somewhat confident, 13% not confident for cash, 16% for repo, 59% of project activity completing after the cash deadline, 51% with no formal contingency plan, 45% still needing more regulatory clarity. Source: SEC press release 2026-111 (sec.gov, Oct 30 2026); DTCC/SIFMA pulse survey (dtcc.com, Sept 22 2026).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The Oct 30 SEC exemptive relief resolves one friction element (pending exemptive relief) but the survey evidence of documentation backlog (59% project activity post-deadline), absence of contingency plans (51%), and residual regulatory-clarity gaps (45%) keeps the indicator squarely in FRICTION (rubric value 1); no deadline extension or operational failure has occurred to warrant escalation to PROBLEMS (2), and readiness is not broad enough to call SMOOTH (0).

oat_bund.fact: As of the 2 November 2026 market open, quifinanza.it reported the OAT-Bund 10-year spread at 164 bps (OAT 4.97%, Bund 3.33%); UBP's Weekly View dated 2 Nov 2026 noted the spread at 161 bps after Moody's held France at Aa3; SP Angel (2 Nov 2026) cited 'c.165bp on Friday [30 Oct]'. Ideal-investisseur.fr (citing Banque de France and Bundesbank) recorded 159.0 bps at the 30 Oct close (OAT 4.93%, Bund 3.34%).
oat_bund.rationale: Multiple Nov 2 sources bracket the spread at 161-165 bps, a re-widening from the 154 bps Oct 26 reading; 163 bps (1.63 percentage points) is the midpoint of corroborated same-week readings. The prior reading of 1.54 is superseded by new post-Oct-26 market data showing a re-widening of approximately 9-11 bps.
oat_bund.change_reason: new_event: post-Oct-26 re-widening; multiple sources on 30 Oct and 2 Nov 2026 place the OAT-Bund spread in the 159-165 bps range, up from 154 bps on 26 Oct, driven by ongoing French fiscal/political risk (budget vote on 3 Nov, S&P review on 27 Nov) even after Moody's held France at Aa3

dissent.view: 159.0 bps at 30 Oct 2026 close, OAT 4.93% vs Bund 3.34% (daily official close reading)
155.6 bps as of 29 Oct 2026 (cbonds daily index)
161 bps for week ending ~31 Oct, after Moody's Aa3 hold brought it down from 174-bp peak (UBP Weekly View, 2 Nov 2026)
